wsl-claude, on one owner-key layer for every VPS device. Today it's NOT orthogonal: three devices, three mechanisms.
1) RELAY: the installer mints an owner invite, shown once over SSH; the first invited claim becomes owner, stored as the FIRST name in allow.json (relayAuth.js:650, ownerName = Object.keys(byName)[0]). Owned by a claim over the wire.
2) FACE PUPPET: relay-state/puppet.json { owner, carries }, written by face-install from the key you type at install (nodeApps.js:218-227). Owned by a file.
3) APP SERVER: learns its owner from the one relay it's pinned to, on its first answer, 'for good' (appServer.js:190-200). Owned by what the relay says.
RECOMMENDATION: yes, one lowest layer. Every public device (relay, face, a peer's print service) keeps ONE file in the same shape, the one puppet.json already has: { owner, carries }. The rules:
- Written only at install, by root over SSH (the box admin is trusted for their own box).
- Afterwards changed only by a command signed by the CURRENT owner (a transfer), never by anything arriving first over the wire.
- Read on every ask, never cached. Missing means owned by nobody, and a device owned by nobody obeys nobody.
The relay can keep its owner invite as the way you PROVE the key at install. Its result just lands in that same file, instead of 'first row of allow.json', which today makes the relay's owner depend on the order of a JSON object.
Small stale thing found: nodeApps.js:226 says a relay box keeps pending-owner.json, but that file was removed in cycle 3 (relayAuth.js:386-391).

wsl-claude, on 'the RAM/disc queries for owners are the same on all server types?': no, not today. Three shapes on three channels, and one device reports nothing:
1) RELAY: pushes 'relay-status' to its owner on the stream (relay.js:4764-4790): process memory, traffic meter, current caps. Box RAM and disk: not included. Its owner is found as the first row of allow.json.
2) APP SERVER: sends a box report by packet (appServer.js:375, 1334): box label, fingerprint, allotted MB, box total MB. Your node collects these in boxes.js (owner.boxSearch / boxGet).
3) YOUR NODE ITSELF: the server-stats job, process memory, kept locally (jobs.js:362).
4) THE FACE PUPPET: reports nothing to its owner.
So the cleanup you want to drive has an obvious shape: one box report, one shape, sent by EVERY owned device to the owner in its one owner file, by packet, and gathered in the boxes.js your node already has. It's the same layer as the owner file: whatever reads { owner } also sends that owner its report. Test I'd hold it to: relay, face and app server each appear in owner.boxSearch with the same fields, and a device whose owner file names someone else never reports to you.

Noted as a cleanup you want to drive: one owner record, read the same way on every server type. Where should it live? It touches relays and puppets, not only faces, so I'd give it its own requirement rather than fold it into G19 next to grantFace. Go! = its own row; I'll draft it here in Team.

Recorded: the owner record comes after grantFace. To start grantFace I need two plain yeses, because two node-interface changes are in it:
1) the verb 'api' (introspection by layers, over peerPost). Is your 'one new verb: api' your yes on it?
2) server processes get the door address, so grantFace can call owner.command.
Go! = yes to both, and I build in the order: api, the door for server processes, grantFace, then its client.
